market_context.summary: The regime is hike risk, not cut hope, and every rate-sensitive long in the book is fighting it. Kalshi prices the 2026-09-16 FOMC at 33-34c for a 25bp HIKE against 0-1c for any cut, with October at 22-23c and December at 24-28c for a hike — essentially zero probability of easing across three consecutive meetings, on real open interest (4.03M contracts on September hold, 1.83M on September hike). The bond market agrees: the 10-year rose to 4.74% from 4.69%, the 2-year to 4.24% from 4.19%, and the 10y-2y curve flattened to +0.46 from +0.50. Core PCE at 3.3% against a 3.63% effective funds rate leaves a real policy rate near 0.3%. The 2026-08-24 tape was a rotation rather than a risk-off day — SPX -0.28%, Nasdaq -0.76%, Dow +0.26% — with memory and AI hardware broken (MU -5.8%, SanDisk -6%, Seagate -6.5%, NVDA -2.91%, MRVL -3.27%) while consumer discretionary ripped (FIVE +5.0%, KSS +4.0%, ULTA +3.3%, ANF +3.1%). Bitcoin is 79,258, up 2.2% in 24 hours and up roughly 26% in nine sessions. The week is front-loaded onto Wednesday: July core PCE at 08:30 ET and NVIDIA's fiscal Q2 after the close, then Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Chair on Friday morning.

catalyst.event: A 50% US tariff on Canadian plywood, wood veneer, laminated veneer lumber and MDF took effect 2026-08-19 under three Section 338 proclamations issued 2026-07-20. Separately, Boise Cascade became sole nationwide distributor of James Hardie s full product portfolio effective 2026-07-31.
catalyst.action: Accumulate in thirds into the 74-80 zone, with the 200-day at 76.71 as the anchor. Add under 70 on any housing-driven flush. There is no need to chase 82; the tariff is a multi-quarter margin change, not a one-day event.

recommendations.thesis: Boise Cascade manufactures exactly the four products Washington just put a 50% tariff on — plywood, veneer, LVL and MDF — and the market has not repriced it: the tariff went live 2026-08-19 and BCC has traded 83.13, 81.77, 82.47, 82.24 since, down 1.1%. The margin arithmetic is already visible before any tariff help, with Wood Products EBITDA at $52.4M in Q2 against $37.3M a year earlier on plywood pricing up 15% y/y; the segment s weak spot was EWP, where I-joist pricing fell 7% and LVL 4% against Canadian import competition that now carries a 50% duty. At $2.90B market cap, ~$148M net debt and ~$505M of annualised Q2 EBITDA, the stock trades near 6.0x EV/EBITDA and 37% below its 18-month high of 131.27.
recommendations.key_risk: Housing demand, which is the whole bear case. Tariffs raise panel prices, but if starts roll over under a Fed that the market gives a one-in-three chance of hiking in September, BCC loses on volume what it gains on price — and its Building Materials Distribution arm, which produced the larger $85.6M of Q2 segment EBITDA, actually pays the higher input costs. Management named volatile mortgage rates as a headwind in the Q2 release.
recommendations.counter_argument: The honest hazard in this specific recommendation is that it converts an existing 81.00 swing long with a 76.00 stop into a stop-free long-term hold, which is the classic way a trader launders a losing trade into an investment. Two things make it defensible here rather than a rationalisation: the position is green, not red, and the thesis genuinely changed after entry — the tariff took effect and the James Hardie agreement began, both after 2026-08-18. The 76.00 stop is being removed deliberately and the invalidation below replaces it. If US housing starts fall more than 10% year-over-year for two consecutive months, or Wood Products segment EBITDA fails to exceed the $52.4M Q2 print in either Q3 or Q4 despite the tariff, the thesis is wrong and the position should be sold regardless of price.

recommendations.thesis: CONTINUING IDEA, RE-LEVELLED. Vistra closed 135.66, 38.3% below its 219.82 high, below its 20-day (143.96), 50-day (153.13) and 200-day (159.58), and 2.3% above its 250-day low of 132.66 — a merchant generator being sold while the load-growth thesis is unchanged and guidance was reaffirmed three weeks ago. Today s work adds the shape of the wider power complex: over 250 sessions the pre-revenue story names have been destroyed — SMR -84.2%, OKLO -79.5%, NNE -70.0%, LEU -61.8% — while businesses that actually generate cash held far better, with CCJ only 24.4% off its high. Vistra sits on the cash-flow side of that split and is being marked as though it sits on the narrative side.
recommendations.key_risk: BEAR-CASE SENSITIVITY, ADDED BY RED TEAM AND THE REASON THIS IS CONVICTION 3, NOT 4. The whole 3.10 ratio rests on a 108 bear case that is asserted rather than derived anywhere in the research. It is load-bearing and it is fragile: at a 104 bear case the ratio falls to 2.58 and at 100 it is 2.21, below the 2.5 floor this report holds long-term ideas to. A 100 handle is not a stretch for a merchant generator in a hiking cycle when the speculative names in the same complex are down 70-85%. Note also that the 128.00 entry sits BELOW the 250-day low of 132.66, so it only fills on a break to new lows — which is the counter-argument below actually happening, not a discount handed over for free. Then rates: this is a capital-intensive generator with real leverage into a market pricing a 33-34% chance of a September hike, zero chance of a cut across three meetings, and a 10-year that rose to 4.74%. Higher discount rates compress exactly this kind of long-duration cash-flow asset, and that is the most likely reason the de-rating runs further before it reverses. With no hard stop, size to survive another 20% drawdown — which is why the entry was moved down rather than the target moved up.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that merchant power margins are cyclical and the datacenter load story is the same story that carried this complex into a bubble which has since lost 70-85% in its speculative names; a 38% de-rating in Vistra may be the first leg of that repricing rather than the end of it. Invalidation, replacing a stop: if Vistra cuts or withdraws its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $6.8-7.6B, or if adjusted FCF before growth comes in below the $3.925B low end for two consecutive quarters, the thesis is wrong and the position should be sold regardless of price.

The specific setup being bought is the familiar pattern where the numbers are fine and the stock still flushes on a guidance nitpick — a move into 190-201 puts it below the 50-day and at the top of the 189.80 120-day low, roughly two ATRs of downside from here, against a 120-day high of 236.54 and sell-side targets clustered $275-325.

Do not treat the entry zone as a value level independent of the numbers. Second, this is the most written-up trade on the street this week — 'buy the post-NVDA flush' is not a differentiated idea, and the only thing keeping it honest is that it costs nothing if the condition never fires. If the market is de-rating AI capex rather than de-risking one print, buying the flush is buying the first leg of a trend. The revenue-and-guide condition on the entry is the guard against exactly that.
